accounting.rationale: PDF128 lines20-23 describes the intended use of the three dummy intents. It does not require every IN dummy to be read or every OUT/INOUT dummy to be assigned.
INTENT describes dummy use, subject to the actual entity categories inC845 and actual/dummy association rules.
Receiving data motivates IN; the normative restrictions and pointer-target distinction are inC846/C847 andp2.
Returning data motivates OUT; p3's entry changes do not require a replacement value to be defined on every invocation.
INOUT permits receiving and returning data but does not require either operation. Definability is required even when the callee does not modify the dummy.
The paragraph crosses PDF128-129. Its nonpointer definition restriction and pointer association restriction are distinct, and the latter contains an express deallocation exception.

Only the stated other-route target deallocation can cause the excepted undefined association. This is not permission to deallocate through the IN pointer or to query the resulting undefined association.
PDF129 lines3-10 contains two entry-state changes, two actual-argument requirements and a whole-invoking-statement interference restriction. Undefined status is not a value or compulsory diagnostic.

Preserve exact7.5.4.6 subcomponent/default-initialization rules, including containing-initialization exclusions. Pointer association and allocation have distinct canonical state/event rules; this is not retention of arbitrary old values.
PDF129 lines11-14 separates ordinary definability from pointer-variable/procedure-pointer eligibility. It does not impose OUT's entry undefinition.
Allocation and definition status, canonical9.7.3.2p6 entry deallocation, and the normativeC848 coarray exclusion are explanatory cross-references, not extra obligations invented from a note.
ALLOCATABLE intent restrictions include allocation status. Initially unallocated status is not the p8 definition of a type having specified default initialization.
Allocation status and definition of allocated data are distinct. ALLOCATED may be meaningful where a payload value is not.
Canonical9.7.3.2p6 and15.5.2.7p7 govern allocated OUT actuals and allocatable subobjects. Do not clone a deallocation/finalization program or query a deallocated payload.
C848 is the numbered owner of the nonintrinsic OUT allocatable-coarray/subobject exclusion.
The MOVE declaration is an incomplete illustration, not a standalone valid program. No missing PERSON definition/body is treated as a standard negative or a new requirement.
The example explains the normative pointer-versus-target distinction. The target is not a subobject of the nonpointer dummy just because a pointer component designates it.
The pointer component as a pointer is a subobject and inherits intent underp6.
The designated target is not that pointer subobject. Target operations still require live association, definability and argument-aliasing conditions.
C847 applies to inherited IN intent in the example's pointer assignment. Do not assign a new note-owned rejection rule.
Intrinsic assignment through the pointer component can define its target without altering pointer association. It is not automatically a forbidden assignment to the IN enclosing object.
The permission expressly requires an associated pointer and a definable target. Undefined/disassociated status, expired targets and other aliasing restrictions are not waived.
Pointer dummy intent likewise restricts association, not all target operations; p2 and15.5.2.8/.10 retain their own actual-category conditions.
The note begins on PDF129 and continues as the separately inventoried note4.2 on PDF130. Possible checking is not automatically mandatory diagnosis.
Documentation is a purpose, not a measurable compulsory execution behavior.
Potential IN checking does not expand4.2's reporting obligations beyond their actual bases.
Preserve the continued note identity and all optional checking/optimization and OUT/INOUT/omitted-intent distinctions, without promoting examples to new normative rules.
A possible before-definition check does not establish a compulsory trap, warning or undefined-value oracle.
An explicit interface can support definability checking; case-specific numbered/scope diagnostic bases remain separate.
Optimization is permitted, not a required code shape, timing, storage operation or elimination result.
OUT does not preserve an unredefined prior value; default initialization and pointer/allocation rules have their own exact premises.
A conditional non-assignment cannot be used to demand old-value retention for OUT. Never execute a later read of such an undefined value as an oracle.
INOUT may be used even when no explicit read occurs, and may leave a defined value unchanged.
No INTENT is not an alias for INOUT; p4 andp5 impose different actual-argument requirements.
For omitted intent, actual use and the effective argument's limitations determine whether definition is allowed. Other pointer, allocation, presence and association restrictions still apply.

requirements.title: An intent specification is IN, OUT or INOUT
requirements.definition: The intent-spec alternatives are IN, OUT and INOUT. Their entity eligibility and semantics are separate from the spelling. INOUT is one alternative, not a comma-separated pair of IN and OUT specifications.

pending.in-admission: PENDING a complete ordinary INTEGER dummy declaration with INTENT(IN), no prohibited definition and a valid explicit interface if invoked. Preserve8.2 and INTENT-statement grammar owners.
pending.out-admission: PENDING INTENT(OUT) on an eligible ordinary dummy, defining it before any read. Syntax admission is not an observation of undefined entry status.
pending.inout-admission: PENDING the INOUT alternative with a definable actual if invoked; no read or write is required merely to demonstrate grammar admission.
pending.malformed-specification: PENDING complete declarations with one invalid intent word or the nonalternative IN,OUT, repaired only to one allowed token. The located cause must concern the intent-spec, not an extra attribute, missing delimiter or generic EOF.

requirements.oracle: Three complete grammar admissions and minimally repaired nonalternatives. Keep syntax, entity role and runtime meaning separate.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Required reporting capability does not prescribe fatal status, exact English or a printed rule number. Case-insensitive spelling retains its lexical owner; unsupported features and unrelated recovery do not qualify.

requirements.title: INTENT is restricted to dummy data objects and dummy procedure pointers
requirements.definition: An entity with INTENT must be a dummy data object or a dummy procedure pointer. An ordinary dummy procedure without POINTER is not the second alternative; neither is a local procedure pointer or ordinary local data variable.

pending.dummy-data-admission: PENDING ordinary data, data POINTER and ALLOCATABLE dummy declarations with independently legal intent/shape/state premises. No C848/C849 or attribute-conflict violation is introduced.
pending.dummy-procedure-pointer-admission: PENDING a genuine dummy PROCEDURE(interface),POINTER with each intent and a complete compatible interface. Do not initialize the dummy, accidentally imply SAVE or invoke it before establishing association.
pending.nondummy-exclusion: PENDING separate ordinary local data and local procedure-pointer INTENT negatives. Repair only by adding the entity to a compatible dummy list or removing INTENT, with no executable use obscuring the entity-role cause.
pending.nonpointer-dummy-procedure-exclusion: PENDING a complete nonpointer dummy procedure with INTENT, repaired only by removing INTENT or by the separately qualified POINTER addition. Preserve characteristics and scope; unsupported procedure-pointer syntax is not a C845 report.

requirements.oracle: Entity-category negatives and minimal controls with precise role diagnostics and legitimate source origins.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No broad 'dummy argument' predicate, fatal-exit promise, unsupported-feature credit or source-line widening. The two allowed categories do not waive their other restrictions.

requirements.title: A nonpointer INTENT(IN) object cannot appear in a variable definition context
requirements.definition: A nonpointer object with IN intent cannot occur in any variable definition context defined by19.6.7. The context list includes syntactic uses that imply definition or undefinition; a branch that would not execute does not remove the syntactic restriction. Pointer target references and inherited subobject intent require their exact separate interpretation.

pending.assignment-and-loop-contexts: PENDING distinct minimal IN-to-INOUT repairs for ordinary assignment, a DO variable and an I/O implied-DO variable, with eligible INTEGER/scalar/rank types. Preserve the statement's own syntax and restrictions.
pending.input-and-internal-output: PENDING direct READ input, a NAMELIST member whose group is used in NML= READ, and CHARACTER internal-file WRITE contexts. The complete negative/control sources include all declarations and valid I/O syntax; an external filename expression is not the internal-file variable context.
pending.io-result-specifiers: PENDING SIZE=, IOMSG=, eligible INQUIRE result specifiers and OPEN NEWUNIT= under their real type/rank/I/O conditions. INQUIRE FILE=, ID= and UNIT= are explicitly excluded from that output-specifier item. Existing I/O owners may supply separately reviewed canonical causes; do not replace the finite list with one assignment.
pending.allocation-output-contexts: PENDING allocate-object, ERRMSG, STAT and NOTIFY-variable contexts from19.6.7p1(9), with each object's actual attribute/type and syntax premises. Do not credit an ALLOCATABLE/POINTER mismatch, unsupported notification or allocation syntax failure as IN-intent diagnosis.
pending.out-inout-association: PENDING a present IN nonpointer object passed to an explicit-interface nonpointer OUT or INOUT dummy. Repair only the incoming intent or the receiving intent as independently valid. A receiver that is a pointer belongs to the association-context analysis, not this item.
pending.associate-selector-propagation: PENDING finite ASSOCIATE, CHANGE TEAM, SELECT RANK and SELECT TYPE selector relations where the associate or one of its subobjects occurs in a variable definition context. Preserve each construct's independent selector/type/rank/coarray requirements and distinguish expression selectors from variables.
pending.coarray-control-contexts: PENDING EVENT POST/WAIT, LOCK/UNLOCK, ACQUIRED_LOCK= and FORM TEAM variables under the actual opaque-type/coarray and scalar LOGICAL premises. Keep C1603-C1614 and image support separate; declaration/control failures cannot be recast as an optional skip for required behavior.
pending.nonpointer-subobjects: PENDING canonical contrasts for an element, substring and nonpointer component inheriting IN underp6. A pointer component's target is not a nonpointer subobject of the enclosing dummy and must not be rejected merely by this analogy.
pending.read-only-controls: PENDING valid references that use the defined incoming data without a definition context, and a complete finite19.6.7 source/use census linking all fifteen context items. Controls are positive-control evidence, not proof of all semantic no-undefinition routes.

requirements.oracle: A finite context census plus isolated syntax/relationship diagnoses with intent-only or receiving-intent repairs. For every case, bind the actual IN object, its context and the precise cause.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The required diagnostic is not necessarily fatal or code-labelled. Generic I/O/type/coarray errors, source echoes, missing-interface recovery and native compiler failures do not qualify. Canonical source-use coverage is not manufactured from one program.

requirements.title: An INTENT(IN) pointer cannot occur in a pointer association context
requirements.definition: An IN pointer is excluded from the pointer association contexts in19.6.8. Those contexts alter the pointer as a pointer; an ordinary definition of its associated definable data target is a different operation.

pending.nullify-context: PENDING NULLIFY of a genuine data or procedure dummy pointer with IN, repaired only to INOUT. Use a compatible explicit interface and no declaration initializer on the dummy.
pending.pointer-assignment-context: PENDING separate data-pointer and procedure-pointer assignment objects, including an inherited IN pointer component underp6. Preserve valid target type/rank/characteristics/lifetime and repair only the intent or the pointer-object relation.
pending.allocate-deallocate-context: PENDING a data dummy pointer as an allocate-object in ALLOCATE and DEALLOCATE, with minimal IN-to-INOUT controls. Do not run an invalid program, demand defined target data after deallocation or credit unrelated allocation-state diagnostics.
pending.pointer-out-inout-actual: PENDING passing the IN pointer to a compatible pointer OUT/INOUT dummy. Preserve the explicit interface and both data/procedure pointer categories; argument-passing requirements and the association-context cause are separately justified.
pending.target-operation-controls: PENDING a live associated INTEGER target modified by intrinsic assignment through the IN pointer, and the corresponding IN enclosing-object pointer-component control. Require independent target values and unchanged defined association; no pointer-target mutation is automatically a prohibited association change.

requirements.oracle: All four19.6.8 context families, narrowly repaired, plus the actual pointer/target boundary. Source and complete-program controls distinguish association from target definition.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No mandatory trap, status or printed code. ASSOCIATED is used only for defined association status. The p2 other-route deallocation exception does not authorize an otherwise forbidden pointer association context.

requirements.title: Nonintrinsic OUT dummies exclude allocatable coarrays and allocatable-coarray subobjects
requirements.definition: An OUT dummy of a nonintrinsic procedure cannot itself be an allocatable coarray or contain a subobject that is an allocatable coarray. Ordinary allocatable objects and eligible nonallocatable coarrays are not excluded merely by this constraint. The nonintrinsic-procedure condition is retained.

pending.allocatable-coarray-dummy: PENDING an otherwise valid ordinary nonintrinsic subprogram with an INTEGER ALLOCATABLE coarray OUT dummy, repaired only to INOUT. Use deferred coshape and the required dummy/interface context; no invocation or image operation is needed for the declaration relationship.
pending.allocatable-coarray-subobject: PENDING a legal derived type with an allocatable-coarray component and a complete OUT dummy declaration, including a separately qualified nested-subobject route. Apply all component and containing-object restrictions, and change only OUT to INOUT. No second opaque-type exclusion may mask the cause.
pending.nonallocatable-coarray-control: PENDING an eligible ordinary INTEGER nonallocatable OUT coarray dummy, with compatible corank/interface if invoked. Nonallocatable is not permission for any arbitrary coarray shape or actual argument.
pending.ordinary-allocatable-control: PENDING an ordinary noncoarray ALLOCATABLE OUT dummy and allocated actual under15.5.2.7. Any entry-deallocation runtime effect retains9.7.3.2 ownership; compile admission is not that effect.
pending.nonintrinsic-boundary-source: PENDING exact intrinsic-interface source relations instead of a fabricated user definition of an intrinsic procedure. The note1 explanation does not broaden the written nonintrinsic condition.

requirements.oracle: Direct/subobject declaration negatives with intent-only repairs and two category controls; keep a capability failure distinct from a qualifying report.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Required reporting has no fatal/text/code mandate. Unsupported coarrays, invalid containing types, missing deferred coshape, descriptor failures or generic OUT errors are not causal C848 evidence.

requirements.title: OUT entities exclude EVENT_TYPE, LOCK_TYPE and NOTIFY_TYPE subcomponents
requirements.definition: An OUT entity cannot be of EVENT_TYPE, LOCK_TYPE or NOTIFY_TYPE from ISO_FORTRAN_ENV, or have a subcomponent of one of those types. The type identity is the intrinsic-module identity, not its local spelling. The rule is not an exemption from the separate named-variable/coarray or variable-definition restrictions.

pending.event-type-out: PENDING an EVENT_TYPE dummy with required coarray form and OUT, repaired only to IN or INOUT. Use a declaration-only complete procedure to avoid additionally violating C1605/C1606 by an actual call or assignment. No private-component or event-count oracle is guessed.
pending.lock-type-out: PENDING the corresponding LOCK_TYPE context underC1607-C1610, with OUT-only repair and no unrelated allocation/type restriction. Intrinsic type identity must survive any local USE rename.
pending.notify-type-out: PENDING the NOTIFY_TYPE context underC1611-C1614. Required Fortran2023 support, the attribute prohibition and a reference compiler's older mode are recorded separately; an unknown intrinsic type is not the intended diagnosis.
pending.nested-subcomponents: PENDING direct and nested nonpointer/nonallocatable containing-type routes for each of the three types, with a coarray containing dummy where required. Do not traverse a pointer target as a subcomponent or introduce an allocatable-coarray subobject that independently violatesC848.
pending.in-inout-controls: PENDING complete IN and INOUT declarations for the qualified type/coarray forms. Invocation, event/lock/notify actions, allocation and extension introduce additional rules and retain their own owners rather than being inferred from declaration admission.

requirements.oracle: Three exact intrinsic-type exclusions and source-qualified nested routes, with minimal intent controls. Declaration-only isolation avoids a competing prohibited actual-argument definition context.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No fatal/text/code mandate, opaque-value guess or byte/layout assumption. A missing coarray attribute, unsupported intrinsic module/type, prohibited actual call or private-component reference is not C849 evidence.

requirements.title: A nonpointer IN dummy is neither defined nor made undefined during invocation and execution
requirements.source: 8.5.10 p2 first sentence, physical PDF128, lines36-37
requirements.definition: Throughout invocation and execution, a nonpointer IN dummy must not be defined or become undefined. This semantic restriction includes invocation and indirect routes, not only explicit assignment syntax. It does not itself require an initially defined value to be referenced, and is not permission to use unavailable data.

pending.defined-read-controls: PENDING meaningful complete positive controls that read defined incoming scalar/array/component data and compute a distinct output with independent literals, without modifying or undefining the IN entity. No empty callee is counted as a universal preservation test.
pending.definition-route-census: PENDING exact canonical C846/19.6.7 and15.5.2.14 relations for direct, forwarded and aliased actions. Retain the numbered owner of a required diagnosis; a semantic violation alone is not an S-level rejection oracle.
pending.undefinition-route-census: PENDING finite19.6.6 invocation/execution routes relevant to an IN dummy, including prohibited forwarding to OUT and allocation/lifetime changes. Do not run an invalid path and then demand a particular value, warning or trap.
pending.allocation-subobject-relations: PENDING exact ALLOCATABLE status and inherited nonpointer-component relations. An unallocated/undefined object cannot be sampled merely because IN exists, and pointer targets are not automatically subobjects.

requirements.oracle: Finite valid-use controls plus canonical source/use and constraint relations. Definedness restrictions are not tested by observing a value after making a program nonconforming.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A specific numbered or scope rule can require reporting; the prose prohibition alone does not. Preserve context-dependent diagnosis and positive-control roles instead of relabelling a read-only admission as a runtime no-undefinition effect.

requirements.title: An IN pointer preserves association except for other-route target deallocation
requirements.source: 8.5.10 p2 second sentence, physical PDF128 lines37-38 through PDF129 lines1-2
requirements.definition: During invocation and execution, an IN pointer dummy's association must not change, except that deallocation of its target by another route may make its association undefined. Intent restricts association, not every operation on the target. A nonpointer actual to an eligible IN pointer dummy follows its own pointer-association route rather than being assigned a fabricated effective argument.

pending.data-association-controls: PENDING a live defined INTEGER target and defined pointer association, checked before/inside/after a meaningful IN-pointer operation with independent values. Canonical C847 operations retain diagnosis ownership; no initial undefined-status inquiry is allowed.
pending.procedure-association-controls: PENDING a compatible procedure pointer and live target, with a legitimate IN dummy call and independent result/event expectations. Host lifetime, characteristics and procedure-pointer actual categories remain15.5.2.10 conditions.
pending.target-definition-controls: PENDING a complete program modifying a definable target through an associated IN pointer, with literal data results and separately established association. Keep a corresponding nonpointer-enclosing-object/pointer-component relation without assuming the target inherits IN.
pending.other-route-deallocation-source: PENDING the exact19.5.2.5p1(3) relation and a valid other-route deallocation context under15.5.2.14. Observe only independently defined allocation/events, never ASSOCIATED or data through the now-undefined pointer. This exception grants no pointer-status value or qualified runtime test of undefinedness.
pending.nonpointer-actual-source: PENDING15.5.2.8p2/15.5.2.10p5 eligible nonpointer actual and target conditions. Under15.5.2.4p5/p6, a data pointer dummy receiving a nonpointer actual is pointer associated but not argument associated; do not silently call that actual its effective argument.

requirements.oracle: Valid association/target controls and separately accounted exception/source relations. Any queried pointer association is independently established as defined.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No undefined-pointer trap/value oracle, no relaxed aliasing rule and no compulsory S-level rejection. The exception does not permit deallocation through the prohibited IN-pointer context itself.

requirements.title: A nonpointer OUT dummy loses definition on invocation except for default-initialized subcomponents
requirements.source: 8.5.10 p3 first sentence, physical PDF129, printed115, lines3-4
requirements.definition: Invocation makes a nonpointer OUT dummy undefined except for its default-initialized subcomponents. The exception uses7.5.4.6's actual subcomponent and containing-initialization rules. It does not preserve arbitrary pre-call values. Allocation status, pointer association and finalization have distinct canonical entry rules.

pending.plain-entry-context: PENDING a context-only complete procedure call with ordinary OUT data, never referencing its old value. A call/event witness may establish that the context occurred, but does not make the unobservable undefined state a runtime effect pass.
pending.default-initialized-exception-source: PENDING source relations to existing S7.5.4.6-003/-004/-005/-006 and their actual OUT-entry witnesses, preserving each original effect owner and role. Distinguish nonpointer data initialization, data/procedure pointer association, nested overriding initializers and7.5.4.6p7 exclusions. Do not clone those programs or retag them context-only to force a link.
pending.allocation-finalization-relations: PENDING exact9.7.3.2p6/15.5.2.7p7 deallocation and S7.5.6.3-007 pre-undefinition finalization relations. Nonpointer nonallocatable and allocatable paths differ; a finalizer may observe valid old data before undefinition, not a callee body after it.
pending.optional-absence-context: PENDING15.5.2.13 presence/absence qualifications: absent optional default initialization has no effect and no absent dummy/subobject is read. Presence guards use real control flow, not assumed logical short circuit.
pending.redefinition-before-use: PENDING context-only controls that assign all subsequently referenced ordinary parts before reading them, with independent result literals. An unredefined OUT actual may not be read by the caller merely to test whether an old bit pattern survived.

requirements.oracle: Context-only execution and canonical source relations, never a prescribed value after undefinition. Actual default-initialization/finalization/deallocation effects retain their own qualified runtime owners.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No negative twin, mandatory warning/trap, zero value, disassociation or physical-storage erasure follows from undefinedness. Source/role relation mechanisms remain pending instead of being bypassed through evidence retagging.

requirements.title: An actual for a nonpointer OUT dummy must be definable
requirements.source: 8.5.10 p3 second sentence, physical PDF129, lines4-5
requirements.definition: An actual argument corresponding to a nonpointer OUT dummy must be definable. Definable is not the same as already defined and is not restricted to an ordinary variable-name spelling; a data-pointer function reference can designate a definable target under19.6.7p2. Other actual/dummy restrictions still apply.

pending.definable-variable-controls: PENDING a complete OUT call using a writable ordinary variable that need not initially be defined, followed by a read only after the callee establishes its value. Use explicit interfaces and independently derived returned literals.
pending.nondefinable-source-contrasts: PENDING exact relations for literals, named constants, expressions and prohibited incoming IN entities. C846 can own the syntactic IN-to-OUT case; other prose violations need their own numbered/scope reporting basis or explicit policy, not universal rejection.
pending.data-pointer-result-target: PENDING a live, associated data-pointer function result used for a nonpointer OUT dummy, where the result designates a definable target and all actual/dummy conditions hold. Contrast with the separate prohibition on passing function-reference results to OUT pointer dummies; do not ban every function reference.
pending.state-presence-and-array-limits: PENDING optional absence, actual pointer allocation/association and array-section/vector-subscript restrictions under15.5.2.4/.5/.7/.13. A definable spelling does not waive rank/type/aliasing rules, and an absent dummy is not accessed.

requirements.oracle: Complete admissible actuals and a source-qualified finite definability relation, with numbered diagnostics retained at their actual owners.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No mandatory prose rejection, blanket function-reference exclusion or read of initially undefined data. A successful call to one writable scalar does not prove all definability contexts.

requirements.title: Invocation gives an OUT pointer dummy undefined association status
requirements.source: 8.5.10 p3 pointer-entry sentence, physical PDF129, lines5-7
requirements.definition: On invocation, an OUT pointer dummy has undefined association status. For a data pointer actual,15.5.2.8p3 explicitly gives the actual the same entry consequence. Undefined association is not the defined state of disassociation and does not by itself deallocate or undefine the former target.

pending.undefined-entry-source: PENDING exact19.5.2.5p1(16) and15.5.2.8p3 source relations for data and corresponding procedure-pointer contexts. No ASSOCIATED inquiry, dereference or target call occurs while association is undefined.
pending.data-pointer-reestablishment: PENDING a context-only complete OUT data-pointer call that first NULLIFYs or pointer-assigns the dummy before any inquiry. Defined post-operation association/data has its canonical NULLIFY/assignment owner, not an invented observation of the prior undefined state.
pending.procedure-pointer-reestablishment: PENDING the analogous procedure-pointer context using a compatible live target or NULLIFY before inquiry/invocation. Preserve procedure characteristics and host lifetime and do not use declaration initialization on a dummy.
pending.former-target-context: PENDING a separate still-live defined target observed by a valid independent name after reestablishing the pointer, under the actual aliasing rules. No automatic deallocation, erasure or guessed pointer bit pattern is inferred from entry association undefinition.

requirements.oracle: Source-bound undefined-state accounting and context-only executions that reestablish status before observation.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No mandatory warning/trap, false ASSOCIATED result, zero address or physical null representation. A post-reassociation pass is not runtime proof of the intermediate undefined association.

requirements.title: OUT pointer actuals are pointer variables or non-result procedure pointers
requirements.source: 8.5.10 p3 pointer-actual sentence, physical PDF129, lines7-8
requirements.definition: An actual corresponding to an OUT pointer dummy must be a pointer variable or a procedure pointer that is not the result of a function reference. Merely being a valid target for an IN pointer dummy does not satisfy this OUT requirement.

pending.data-pointer-variable: PENDING an actual data pointer variable with matching type/rank/parameters and a complete OUT dummy interface. The callee establishes association before any inquiry; old association need not be sampled.
pending.procedure-pointer-variable: PENDING a named compatible procedure pointer actual, reestablished before invocation/query in the OUT callee. Preserve characteristic and host-instance requirements.
pending.function-result-exclusion-source: PENDING source-qualified contrasts for data/procedure pointer function results, with otherwise identical interfaces and targets. This is not the nonpointer-dummy case where a data-pointer result can designate a definable target. No mandatory diagnosis is inferred without its separate basis.
pending.target-and-null-expression-boundaries: PENDING the exact differences between a nonpointer target, NULL() expression and a pointer variable whose status is disassociated. Do not substitute IN's nonpointer-target permission or confuse a null expression with a pointer variable.

requirements.oracle: Finite admitted pointer-variable contexts and explicit source restrictions on result/target/expression alternatives.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No blanket required rejection of prose violations and no association inquiry before status is established. Nonpointer OUT and pointer OUT actual rules are not merged.

requirements.title: OUT association changes cannot affect another entity in the invoking statement
requirements.source: 8.5.10 p3 final sentence, physical PDF129, lines8-10
requirements.definition: Definition or undefinition implied by associating an actual with an OUT dummy must not affect another entity within the statement invoking the procedure. Both induced definition and induced undefinition matter; the scope is the whole invoking statement, not only the invoked body or one written argument.

pending.invoking-statement-use-census: PENDING an exact source/use relation for OUT calls in CALL statements and function-reference statements, accounting for other arguments, selectors and expression entities. Record overlaps with15.5.2.14 and expression restrictions rather than inventing a single causal diagnostic for aliased invalid programs.
pending.default-initialization-interference: PENDING the entry definition/default-initialization side, not only loss of old values. Use the real7.5.4.6 and19.6.5 event relations and keep inherited/nested subcomponent conditions explicit.
pending.deallocation-finalization-relations: PENDING exact entry deallocation/finalization and association-induced definition/undefinition relationships. Other callback side effects retain their own rules; do not claim every side effect is literally this clause's association event.
pending.independent-precomputed-controls: PENDING complete admissible programs that use separate defined actuals or precompute needed values in prior statements, with independent literal/event expectations and valid aliasing. They are positive controls, not a forced outcome for a violating same-statement program or an imposed argument-evaluation order.

requirements.oracle: Finite whole-statement source/use accounting and valid independent-entity controls. A nonconforming interference path has no required runtime value.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No compulsory trap/rejection and no assumed left-to-right evaluation, short circuit or copy timing. Required diagnosis from some overlapping numbered rule remains with that rule.

requirements.title: A nonpointer INOUT dummy always requires a definable actual
requirements.source: 8.5.10 p4 first sentence, physical PDF129, lines11-12
requirements.definition: An actual corresponding to a nonpointer INOUT dummy must be definable, even if that invocation never writes the dummy. INOUT does not impose OUT's entry undefinition. Definability alone does not assert that all data are initially defined or permit reading an undefined part.

pending.definable-actual-controls: PENDING ordinary writable scalar/array actuals and a separately qualified data-pointer function-result target. Match type/rank/interface and preserve the distinct pointer-dummy actual rule.
pending.nonmodifying-inout-source: PENDING exact literals/constants/expressions contrasts even for a callee that only reads or does nothing. A read-only branch cannot turn INOUT into omitted intent; required diagnostics need their actual numbered/scope basis or a separate policy.
pending.partial-definition-and-retention: PENDING complete controls that retain an already defined value on a nonwriting path and define any initially undefined part before reading it on a writing path. Independent literals and event guards prevent no-op evidence, without asserting that INOUT always reads or always changes its argument.
pending.optional-and-attribute-boundaries: PENDING explicit15.5.2.4/.6/.7/.13 relations for absent OPTIONAL and eligible ALLOCATABLE actuals. There is no access to an absent/unallocated payload and no automatic OUT-style deallocation imported into INOUT.

requirements.oracle: Finite admissible definable-actual controls and source-qualified unconditional definability, with separate definedness premises for every read.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No mandatory prose rejection, guarantee of a write, initially defined-value requirement or blanket ban on data-pointer function references. Controls retain positive-control roles.

requirements.title: INOUT pointer actuals have the pointer-variable restriction
requirements.source: 8.5.10 p4 second sentence, physical PDF129, lines12-14
requirements.definition: An INOUT pointer dummy requires a pointer variable or a procedure pointer that is not a function-reference result as its actual. IN's qualified nonpointer-target alternatives do not apply. Unlike OUT, INOUT does not itself make a previously defined association status undefined on entry.

pending.data-pointer-variable: PENDING matching data-pointer actual/dummy variables with deliberately established association or disassociation. Observe only valid states, then use canonical pointer assignment to rebind if required by the positive control.
pending.procedure-pointer-variable: PENDING compatible procedure-pointer variables with live target/host and explicit interface. A callback has independent result/event expectations and no declaration initializer on a dummy.
pending.function-result-exclusion-source: PENDING the separate data/procedure function-result restrictions and a minimally contrasting pointer-variable context. The prose restriction does not by itself demand rejection, and the nonpointer INOUT target interpretation is not this case.
pending.nonpointer-target-boundary: PENDING a finite15.5.2.8/.10 source relation contrasting IN's eligible nonpointer target with INOUT's actual-pointer condition, including the distinct NULL() expression and disassociated pointer variable.

requirements.oracle: Admitted pointer-variable controls and exact source-bound result/target exclusions; meaningful observations occur only at defined association states.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No arbitrary undefined-association query, universal target mutability, compulsory S-level rejection or duplicate pointer-assignment effect claim.

requirements.title: Omitted INTENT leaves use constrained by the effective argument
requirements.definition: When a dummy has no INTENT attribute, its use remains subject to the limitations of its effective argument. Omission is not INOUT: an ordinary read-only use can admit an actual that would fail INOUT's unconditional definability requirement. Pointer, allocatable, presence and other argument rules are not waived.

pending.read-only-expression-actual: PENDING a complete ordinary nonpointer no-INTENT dummy reading a defined scalar literal/expression actual and producing an independent result. Keep a compatible explicit interface and no definition, undefinition or unavailable inquiry of that effective argument.
pending.conditional-definition-controls: PENDING separate admissible invocations where a readonly path receives a defined expression and a writing path receives a definable variable, with explicit control flow and independent expected values/events. Never run the writing path on the expression and prescribe a failure.
pending.omitted-versus-inout-source: PENDING exact source/canonical relations to S8.5.10-008 showing why a nonwriting INOUT invocation still needs a definable actual. No mandatory diagnosis is invented from this explanatory contrast.
pending.effective-argument-category-census: PENDING15.5.2.4's precise effective-argument definition and finite VALUE, pointer, allocatable, OPTIONAL and forwarding restrictions. Omitted intent on a pointer does not gain IN's nonpointer-actual allowance, and the anonymous VALUE object's definability has its own owner.

requirements.oracle: Meaningful complete valid-use controls with source-qualified effective-argument and conditional-definition relations.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No universal equivalence to INOUT, unconditional permission to mutate expressions or warning/trap for invalid use. Logical short circuit, argument evaluation order and unspecified copy behavior are not assumed.

requirements.title: All subobjects of a nonpointer object inherit its INTENT
requirements.definition: Every subobject of a nonpointer object with INTENT has that same INTENT. A pointer component as a pointer is a subobject; the target it designates is not. Consequently inherited IN can forbid reassociating that component while allowing definition of an associated definable target.

pending.elements-and-substrings: PENDING exact array-element/section and character-substring source relations with complete C846 negative/repair controls. Subscript/substring bounds and rank/type rules must remain independently valid.
pending.derived-and-allocatable-components: PENDING direct and nested nonpointer components and an ALLOCATABLE component's status/data restrictions. A component with its own default initialization is not a waiver of IN; OUT entry events retain their initialization/deallocation owners.
pending.pointer-subobject-target-boundary: PENDING paired C847 reassociation negative and valid target-definition control through a pointer component of a nonpointer IN dummy. Establish a live, associated, definable target and preserve15.5.2.14; do not make pointer targets inherit the containing object's intent.
pending.canonical-inherited-intent-census: PENDING a finite source/use inventory joining actual subobject categories to C846/C847 and OUT/INOUT actual/entry owners, with each original primary owner and evidence role preserved. An INTENT inquiry intrinsic or a no-op classifier is not invented.

requirements.oracle: Source-qualified inherited-attribute relations and meaningful canonical negative/control contexts. Pointer association and target data definition remain separately judged.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Required diagnosis arises from an applicable numbered/scope rule, not automatically every prose relation. No pointer-target-as-subobject shortcut, broader pure-procedure restriction or evidence-role bypass.
